title.title: Kurosh's problem fails for division rings
title.subtitle: Claim: a division ring algebraic over its centre, generated by two elements, yet infinite-dimensional

plain: A number system where every element solves some polynomial, yet two elements generate infinitely much

lines.tex: D \text{ a division ring}, \;\; F = Z(D)
\text{every } x \in D \text{ is algebraic over } F

beats.text: Kurosh asked in 1941: if every element is algebraic, is the ring locally finite?
Golod and Shafarevich said no for algebras in 1964; division rings stayed open
The claim: two generators, every element algebraic, infinite dimension

steps: Start with two generators inside a division algebra
Step by step, solve equations that make each new element algebraic
In the limit: all algebraic, yet infinite-dimensional

achievement.label: Kurosh's problem for division rings (1941)
statement: D \text{ algebraic over } Z(D) \;\Longrightarrow\; D \text{ locally finite}
achievement.context: Known in many cases, such as PI division rings and uncountable centres
achievement.note: Countable, characteristic 0; built by solving free-series equations step by step

verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and the review; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Kurosh, nineteen forty-one: must algebraic division rings be locally finite?
Solve equations step by step, so that in the limit every element is algebraic.
Claimed: two generators, infinite dimension, all algebraic.

sources.quote: Kurosh asked in 1941 whether an algebra that is algebraic over its centre is locally finite. Golod and Shafarevich answered no for algebras in 1964, but the division-ring case stayed open.
locally finite in many cases (e.g. PI division rings, uncountable centres)
The paper claims a countable division ring of characteristic 0 that is algebraic over its centre and generated by two elements, yet infinite-dimensional.
A Lean directory named `Kurosh` exists, but there is no Comparator entry or scope note for this family, so I treat it as unformalized.
